evals.prompt: I'm an org admin and just installed kei. Show me the safe sequence to create a runtime installation for a local coding harness, get its credential into our secret manager, and check its status. Don't make up commands for creating a workspace.
evals.expected_output: Logs in first with the device flow, uses kei bot init --platform cli, pipes kei bot credential to a secret manager, uses kei bot status, and says workspaces are created in the web app.
expectations: kei login is run before any kei bot command and the response notes a person must approve it in the browser.

Every kei command used is one of: kei login, kei logout, kei setup, kei runtime bootstrap, kei upgrade, kei bot init, kei bot credential, kei bot agents, kei bot status, kei bot bind, kei bot delete, kei help, kei --version (no invented subcommands such as kei workspace, kei runtime tokens, or kei bot list).
The response explicitly says the CLI does not manage organizations or workspaces.

evals.prompt: The runtime is pending after deployment and I want to diagnose it without changing cloud resources. What should I inspect and what evidence should I collect?
evals.expected_output: Provides read-only CLI status and local/provider checks, distinguishes pending heartbeat from a failed deployment, and avoids credential disclosure.
expectations: The response treats a pending status as evidence about heartbeat rather than proof that the runtime is healthy.
The response does not suggest printing or pasting a runtime credential.

evals.prompt: I want to run `kei policy list` and `kei policy update` for a workspace. What should you verify before using those commands?
evals.expected_output: Checks the installed CLI help and governed contract first, explains that current releases may not provide these commands, and routes unsupported resource management to the Kei API skill without inventing endpoints.
expectations: The response does not claim a future resource command exists without source or help evidence.
The response mentions opaque pagination and PATCH/update-mask semantics only as contract requirements for a released resource command.

evals.prompt: kei bot status --installation 3f2c9a1e-8b7d-4c6e-9f10-2a3b4c5d6e7f says 'not logged in; run kei login first' but I logged in yesterday against staging. what's going on
evals.expected_output: Explains the token is short-lived and bound to the API URL host; log in again.
expectations: The response explains the login token is short-lived or expires.
The response says the token is per environment and login again is needed.

evals.prompt: I want our coding agent to use the kei CLI to check whether it's allowed to open a PR before it does. What command should the agent run?
evals.expected_output: Says the kei CLI is for platform admins, not agent run-time checks; points to kei-proxy authorize and the kei-proxy skill.
expectations: The response says the kei CLI is the platform admin CLI and is not how an agent checks permission at run time.
The response names kei-proxy authorize as the per-call check.

evals.prompt: I ran `kei login` and the browser opened to the Kei Dashboard instead of the approval page. The CLI is just sitting there waiting. What went wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the user was not signed in at app.haikeilabs.com first, so the SSO flow lost the return address (HAI-370). Tells them to sign in first, then run kei login again and approve on the 'Kei CLI approved' page.
expectations: The response identifies that the user needs to sign in at app.haikeilabs.com before running kei login.
The response mentions the lost return address or HAI-370 as the root cause.
The response tells the user to run kei login again after signing in.

evals.prompt: During `kei login` on macOS I got a dialog that says 'Keychain Not Found' for app.haikeilabs.com. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: Explains HOME is overridden so macOS cannot find ~/Library/Keychains. Recommends running kei with real HOME or symlinking sandbox/Library/Keychains to real keychain. Warns to click Cancel, not Reset To Defaults.
expectations: The response identifies that HOME being overridden is the cause.
The response recommends running kei with the real HOME or creating a symlink for the sandbox keychain.
The response warns to click Cancel and not Reset To Defaults.

evals.prompt: I tried to approve `kei login` but the page says '403 organization owner or admin role is required'. What does this mean?
evals.expected_output: Explains only org owners and admins can approve the device flow. A member role or unauthenticated user is refused. Tells the user to ask an org owner or admin to run and approve kei login instead.
expectations: The response explains that only org owners and admins can approve the login flow.
The response says a member role gets this error.
The response tells the user to ask an org owner or admin to run kei login and approve it.

evals.prompt: I ran `kei runtime bootstrap` on macOS and got 'mkdir /var/lib/kei-proxy: permission denied'. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: Explains that kei-proxy defaults to a Linux-style state directory that does not exist on macOS. Recommends setting KEI_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR to a user-writable directory with 0700 permissions. Mentions HAI-374 as the underlying bug.
expectations: The response identifies that the default state directory /var/lib/kei-proxy is not writable on macOS.
The response recommends setting KEI_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR to a user-writable path.
The response mentions creating the directory with chmod 0700.
The response references HAI-374 as the known bug.

evals.prompt: I ran `kei policies list --workspace my-workspace` and got a JSON decode error instead of my policies. kei --version says 0.1.10. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains that kei ≤ 0.1.10 sent a malformed request causing a decode error (HAI-373). Recommends upgrading to kei v0.1.11+ or using the web app. Notes that after upgrading, policies commands accept names in addition to IDs.
expectations: The response identifies that kei ≤ 0.1.10 has a bug that causes the decode error.
The response recommends upgrading kei to v0.1.11 or later.
The response mentions using the web app as an alternative.
The response references HAI-373 as the known bug.
The response notes that after upgrading, policies commands accept a policy name in addition to ID.
